title: Checkout loop: scratch anchors and pre-merge playbook
content:
Context:
Quick informal scratchpad for myself while triaging the "checkout-loop" change set. Goal is to have a lightweight, low-friction pre-merge checklist + short runnable probes so we can merge smaller increments safely and avoid late rollbacks. Notes are intentionally terse — for capture and iteration.

High-level hypothesis:
- The PR reduces KV cache lock contention by sharding the cache per-stream instead of global LRU. Should lower tail latency under bursty chat workloads but may increase memory pressure.
- Risk surface: memory growth, cold-start penalties, cross-request cache misses, and subtle race during shutdown.

Quick triage (5–10m):
- Does CI pass? Unit tests + basic integration smoke? (yes/no)
- Any new flaky test patterns in logs? grep for "timeout"/"OOM"/"race"
- Primary changed modules: kv/cache.go, stream/session.go, shutdown/teardown.go -> skim for obvious panics or deferred unlocking patterns
- Check PR description for migration steps and toggles (feature flags)

Pre-merge checklist (must-haves before merge):
- [ ] CI green (unit + integration). If flakes in integration, capture log snippet and mark as "investigate post-merge" only if risk is small.
- [ ] Add short e2e script that can be run locally (see runnable steps below).
- [ ] Add a feature flag: kv_shard_strategy=per_stream (default off) + rolling rollout plan in PR notes.
- [ ] Memory regression test: run loadbench for 10 min with worst-case sequence length (2048) and capture RSS. Compare to baseline.
- [ ] Add metrics: kv_shard_count, kv_shard_size_bytes (hist), kv_evictions, kv_hit_rate_by_key_prefix. Confirm exported in current Prometheus metrics.
- [ ] Update tracing spans to include shard id for expensive ops (helpful for post-merge debugging).
- [ ] Document fallback: on OOM or >10% mem increase, auto-disable feature flag and fallback to global LRU variant.

Runnable probes (local / cluster small-scale):
- Local smoke (single dev machine):
  1) ./dev/run_inference --model llama-mini --sequence 2048 --concurrency 16 --duration 120s
  2) Toggle kv_shard_strategy at start (env var) and compare tail latency p95/p99.
  3) watch "ps -o rss -p <pid>" and prometheus exporter endpoints (/metrics) for kv_shard_size_bytes

- Cluster probe (staging):
  1) Canary 5% traffic to a dedicated pool with shards enabled. Use synthetic chat workloads: 20% short, 60% medium, 20% long sequences.
  2) Observe: p50/p95/p99 latency, mem RSS across nodes, number of evictions, and OOM kills for 30m.
  3) If memory increases > 12% on average or p99 latency regresses > 20% -> rollback.

Refactor ideas (mini PR suggestions to split risk):
- Split A: Introduce an interface KVCacheManager with two implementations (GlobalLRU, ShardedPerStream). Keep feature flag wiring in a single config adapter. This isolates behavior and simplifies toggle.
- Split B: Move shard allocation logic into its own small package (kv/shard_alloc). Keep heavy concurrency primitives encapsulated and unit-tested.
- Split C: Add a lightweight mem-guard wrapper that tracks per-shard approximate byte usage and signals eviction proactively instead of waiting for global pressure.

Edge cases and unresolved questions (to answer in follow-ups):
- How does shard strategy behave for long-lived streams vs short-lived ephemeral requests? Do we need TTL eviction per-shard?
- What happens to cross-request dedupe scenarios that previously benefited from a global cache? Are we intentionally accepting dedupe loss? Document tradeoff.
- Is the shard count static (N based on CPU) or adaptive (based on concurrency)? If adaptive, need smoothing to avoid hot re-sharding storms.

Monitoring & post-merge playbook:
- Alerts to create/verify before merge:
  - kv_hit_rate drop > 15% sustained 5m -> pager (P2).
  - per-node RSS increase > 15% vs baseline -> page ops on call.
  - p99 tail latency increase > 25% compared to baseline -> page SRE.
- Dashboards to watch: per-route latency, per-model memory, kv_evictions over time, pod restarts.
- Post-merge immediate checklist (first 2h):
  - 5m: confirm canary not OOMing, evictions within expected range.
  - 30m: compare p99 vs baseline, confirm no customer errors uptick.
  - 2h: decision point to widen rollout or rollback.

Rollback steps (pre-encoded so ops can act fast):
- Flip feature flag to false via config service -> triggers fallback to GlobalLRU path.
- If service instability persists, scale down canary and route remaining traffic to previous revision (k8s rollout undo).
- If memory leak suspected and flag flip insufficient, redeploy previous image.

Suggested PR description template (short):
- TL;DR: Shard KV cache per-stream to reduce lock contention and lower tail latency under high concurrency. Feature-flagged off by default.
- Changes: list files and short one-liners.
- Risk: memory regression, dedupe loss across streams, shutdown race.
- Safety: feature flag, canary rollout, metrics + auto-fallback on mem/latency thresholds.
- How to test locally: include the runnable probe commands above.

Notes to self (random):
- If we add per-shard histograms, keep cardinality low: shard id + bucketed size (small/med/large) rather than raw key.
- Consider an eviction policy that prefers per-stream short-lived entries first to preserve long-lived session KV.
- Revisit test coverage: add a deterministic unit test that simulates concurrent writes and ensures no double-free/unlocked states on shutdown.

Followups / TODO (convert to tickets later):
- [ ] Small PR: extract KVCacheManager interface + wiring (target: <1 day).
- [ ] Small PR: add mem-guard wrapper + unit tests (target: 2 days).
- [ ] Create INF ticket for canary rollout plan and thresholds (INF-6782 placeholder).
- [ ] Add Prometheus metrics + tracing span update (instrumentation task).

Open questions for the author (ask in PR comment):
- Can we sketch the expected mem delta (ballpark MB/node) for +1 shard per core? Even rough numbers help SRE.
- Are there any customers currently using global dedupe patterns we need to notify?

End of scratch notes. Keep this doc as short-lived; move actionable items to tickets and keep the PR description concise.

-- E.C.
